> 豐。亨，王假之；勿憂，宜日中。

Hexagram 55 is about abundance, and its character means a vessel loaded with offerings.

## 豐 is 豆之豐滿

Built on 豆, the ritual vessel. 說文: 豐，豆之豐滿者也 — the fullness of what is in the vessel.

So the original sense is a vessel filled with offerings. Not "great."

And "great" is an extension — a full vessel holds much, and much is large.

Which matters, because the fullness in the original sense is exactly what the hexagram warns about.

## 假 is 至

王假之 — 假 is to arrive, to reach. Not "borrow."

The same usage as in 王假有廟 in 萃 and 渙: a king arriving at a place.

So the king has arrived at this condition — the condition of being full.

勿憂，宜日中 — do not worry, and it is fitting at noon.

Noon is when the sun is highest, and the hexagram says to be there then, and not to be anxious. Which is the strangest consolation in the book: the moment of fullness is correct, and it is also the moment right before the decline.

## 蔀: a bigger and bigger mat

蔀 is a covering, a mat of grass and reeds, extended to "that which obscures."

Note the grammar: 豐 here is a verb — to make abundant, to enlarge.

So 豐其蔀 is: make the covering larger.

And the three lines read as one action: thickening the obscuration, layer after layer.

## 日中見斗 / 日中見沫

斗: the Dipper. 沫: tiny stars (one reading, 昧, dim).

At noon, seeing the Dipper — a total eclipse, stars visible in daylight.
At noon, seeing only faint points — the darkness has gone deeper.

So the hexagram's picture of abundance at its peak is an eclipse: the light is at its highest, and something has covered it.

## 夷主

夷: level, plain. 夷主 — a master who treats one levelly, a plain and constant lord.

Set against 初九's 配主 — a master who matches me. One is about equality, one about plainness.

And the fourth line, in the middle of the eclipse, meets the 夷主 and the verdict is 吉. Which says where the recovery comes from: not from more light, from a level person.

## 闃其無人

Top line: 豐其屋，蔀其家，闃其無人.

To make the house large, to cover the household, and it is silent with nobody in it.

Three characters for silence. The full vessel, the big roof, and no one inside.

## 折獄致刑

The 象: 君子以折獄致刑.

折 is to judge; 獄 is the case; 致 is to apply.

The 象 reads this out of the trigrams: lightning for clarity (seeing the facts) and thunder for weight (deciding the penalty).

So a hexagram about abundance ends with the administration of justice, which is the one place where fullness must not be decorative.

## The test

Take a peak you are at or have been at — a company, a career, a body of work. Ask the hexagram's question: what is the 蔀 — what has been growing over the light while the light was rising? The eclipse in this chapter is not caused by the sun.
